entities.notes: Sample entity 'Apollo 11 sample 10084'. Landing/mission facts confirmed via NASA NSSDCA and Lunar Sample Compendium (Meyer 2009). CRITICAL FINDING: all 11 stored oxide values are an EXACT match (every digit) to Lunar Sourcebook Table 7.15 column '11', whose own footnote states this column is 'Composition of soil 10002 from Apollo 11 site' — NOT 10084. 10002 and 10084 are two different splits of the same original scoop (per LSC_10084.pdf's own introduction, '10002 was similar soil picked up at the same time... analyses indicate it is of similar composition'), so this is a mislabeled-but-closely-related source, not a random error. Independently, a genuine 10084-specific analysis (Agrell et al. 1970, in LSC_10084.pdf Table 1a) corroborates 9 of the 11 oxides to the source's own rounding; only Cr2O3 has no dedicated 10084 analysis anywhere in the accessible documents. Stored mineral percentages (Plagioclase/Pyroxene/Olivine/Ilmenite/Agglutinates/Glass/Other) do not match the only real modal analysis of 10084 we could find (Simon et al. 1981, reproduced in both LSC_10084.pdf and Lunar Sourcebook Table 7.2), which uses partly different categories and very different numbers. Stored coordinates (0.6875, 23.4333) do not match the current authoritative LM position (NSSDCA/LROC 0.67416N, 23.47314E, or Davies & Colvin 2000: 0.67408N, 23.47297E); per the-moon.us they trace to an old Wikipedia figure whose source is explicitly 'unknown'.

entities.notes: Sample entity 'Apollo 12 sample 12070'. LSC_12070.pdf (Meyer 2011) states 12070 is actually the CONTINGENCY sample, collected in front of the LM at the very start of EVA-1 — not from the ALSEP site as stored sample_description claims. CRITICAL FINDING: all 11 stored oxide values are an EXACT match to Lunar Sourcebook Table 7.15 column '12', whose footnote states this column is an 'Average composition of selected soils (12001, 12023, 12030, 12032, 12033, 12037, 12041, 12042, 12044, 12070) from the Apollo 12 site' — a 10-sample site average, not an analysis of 12070 alone (12070 is only 1 of the 10 contributing soils). Stored coordinates DO match the current NSSDCA/LROC value exactly. Stored mineral percentages do not match either 1971 modal analysis of 12070 found in LSC_12070.pdf (Frondel et al. 1971; McKay et al. 1971).

check.notes:
I checked every claim against the saved documents, reading page images to confirm table columns: LSC 10084/12070/14163 Table 1a, Lunar Sourcebook Tables 7.2 (p.291), 7.15 (p.346) and 7.16 (p.347), and Apollo 12 PSR Table 12-VII (p.205). The reader's column readings are correct: Agrell70 for 10084, Compston71 for 12070, Rose72 for 14163. The stored oxide sets exactly equal Lunar Sourcebook Table 7.15 columns 11, 12 and 14.

What the reader got wrong:
(1) Cr2O3 was marked not_found for all three samples, but documents state it for each. For 10084 it is 0.290 wt% (LSB Table 7.16), which supports the stored 0.3. For 14163 it is 0.200 wt% (LSB Table 7.16), and for 12070 it is 0.41 wt% (Apollo 12 PSR Table 12-VII); both differ from the stored values.
(2) For 14163, FeO, MnO and Na2O were marked 'differs' even though Rose72 equals the stored values.
(3) For 14163, the Olivine 0.4 and Pyroxene 4.1 values from Carr and Meyer (1972) on LSC p.1 were missed. Simon's '2.6 pyroxene' is actually pyroxene plus olivine combined (LSB Table 7.2).
(4) The mineral:Other values for all three samples are the reader's own sums of other categories, not values any source states.
(5) The 14163 description says 'Comprehensive', but 14259 is the Apollo 14 comprehensive sample; 14163 is the bulk soil sample (Apollo 14 PSR Table 5-III).
(6) The 10084 coordinates 0.6875/23.4333 do have a source: ALSJ lists them as the Apollo-era LM position. They are superseded by the LROC position (0.67416/23.47314), but not unsourced.

One decision for the owner: each Cr2O3 value comes from a different analysis than the one the reader used for the other oxides. If every composition must come from one analysis, there are two options. Either keep the Agrell70 / Compston71 / Rose72 tables and leave Cr2O3 empty, or switch the whole table to an analysis that includes Cr2O3: Papike 1982 for 10084 and 14163, LSPET70 for 12070. Those alternatives have no P2O5. For the mineral fields, none of the stored numbers is supported by any document. I searched every local source and did one web search. The source schemes don't match the stored categories, so the owner's rule means leaving them empty rather than forcing a match. Everything I opened is under /Volumes/Extreme SSD/Spring - Forest on the moon/DIRT/Sources/papers/ (lunar/ and LRS/).

reading.notes:
Scope note: the harness task named A11, A12, A14 as the three entities to verify (site-level Apollo 11/12/14 landing-site rows). Only these three were audited; the sample-level entities 10084/12070/14163 that appear in the same JSON file were not in scope per the relayed instruction and were left untouched.

Overall pattern across all three sites: date, lat/lng and both description claims per site trace cleanly to named, saved documents (NASA NSSDCA master-catalog pages, the-moon.us pages citing Davies and Colvin 2000, and the three Apollo Preliminary Science Reports, SP-214/235/272, all fetched from apollojournals.org's ALSJ mirror and saved under Sources/papers/lunar/). samples_returned matches a widely used PSRD/Lunar-Sample-Compendium mission-mass table (34.3 kg / 42.3 kg) for A12/A14 but not for A11 (21.5 vs 21.55/21.8 kg in every source found).

The four geotechnical fields (bulk_density, friction_angle, cohesion, bearing_capacity) are the weak spot for all three sites: no single document states any of the site-level stored numbers as a point value. Lunar Sourcebook Tables 9.4 and 9.11 and the Apollo PSRs themselves only ever give ranges or differently-defined quantities (e.g. 'static bearing pressure' vs 'bearing capacity'). Per the owner's 'empty over wrong' rule, I would drop bearing_capacity for A11/A12 (stored numbers conflate applied pressure with bearing capacity) and drop or replace A14's cohesion (0.18 kPa contradicts every source, all of which explicitly call Apollo 14 trench cohesion unusually low, <0.1 kPa) rather than show them uncited. bulk_density/friction_angle/cohesion for the other cells fall inside at least one cited range (range_only) and could be shown as that range with its reference, but not as the current precise numbers.

All source documents were saved under /Volumes/Extreme SSD/Spring - Forest on the moon/DIRT/Sources/papers/lunar/ (PSR PDFs, NSSDCA/the-moon.us/PSRD/LROC/NASA-curator HTML+txt pairs) or already existed there (Lunar Sourcebook PDF in Sources/papers/LRS/, Gasteiner Dataset_Regolith.csv). The Gasteiner et al. 2026 paper PDF itself (Sources/papers/LRS/) does not contain the per-site numeric tables; those live only in its companion GitHub dataset (github.com/leoniegasteiner/Lunar-Regolith-Database), which I downloaded and saved as Gasteiner_OpenDatabase_Dataset_Regolith.csv — this was essential for tracing the site geotechnical rows to their named primary sources (Costes et al. 1971, Jaffe 1973, Carrier et al. 1972b/1973c, the three Apollo PSRs, etc.), confirming the task's expectation that the paper's open dataset, not the paper text, carries the per-value provenance.

Two small housekeeping notes: I found (and removed) exact duplicate NSSDCA/ALSJ files this session had already fetched with different names in an earlier pass on A15-A17; the surviving Sources/papers/lunar/ files use the *_Apollo11/12/14_* naming used above. I did not touch Sources/papers/lunar/LSC_10084.pdf, LSC_12070.pdf or LSC_14163.pdf substantively — their compendium 'Introduction' sections describe the sample, not mission-level site facts (landing date/coordinates/mass), so they were not usable for the site-level fields being checked here; they remain relevant for the sample entities (10084/12070/14163) if those are audited later.

check.notes:
I re-opened every document myself from Sources/papers/lunar and Sources/papers/LRS: the NSSDCA and the-moon.us pages, the ALSJ table, all three PSRs, the Gasteiner CSV, the PSRD, Curator, LROC and NASA pages. The Lunar Sourcebook text layer has no Table 9.4 or 9.11 content, so I rendered PDF pages 507, 530 and 531 and read the tables from the images. All reference mention quotes occur.

Three changes to the reader's result:
(1) A11 samples_returned is REFUTED. A NASA JSC curation abstract (Allton 2009, hosted on nasa.gov) states '58 samples weighing 21.5 kg collected on Apollo 11', so the stored value is supported. I saved it as /Volumes/Extreme SSD/Spring - Forest on the moon/DIRT/Sources/papers/lunar/NASA_Allton2009_LunarSamples_ApolloCollectionTools.pdf, with a .txt copy.
(2) A12 bulk_density is REFUTED. The Apollo 12 PSR p.182 gives a site-specific in situ value of 1.8±0.2 g/cc from the cores. The reader said the PSR only gives 1.5.
(3) A14 bulk_density is CONFIRMED with a caveat. The Apollo 14 PSR p.95 also states averages of 1.87 and 1.79 g/cm³ from MET tracks. The Lunar Sourcebook says that method estimates relative density better than bulk density, so I do not propose 1.87 as a correction.

All the reader's 'differs' and 'range_only' calls for friction angle, cohesion and bearing capacity hold. None of the stored point values 1.61, 40.7, 1.06, 10, 31.8, 1.04, 8.5, 1.54, 39 or 0.18 is stated in any document I opened.

Small location errors: the A11 PSR 'first manned lunar landing' sentence is on p.85, the A11 bearing-capacity passage is on p.108, and the A12 'Intrepid landed' sentence is on p.113. The Lunar Sourcebook DOI given (10.1016/0031-9201(92)90060-9) probably points to a 1992 PEPI review, not the book.

entities.notes: Apollo 15 - Hadley-Apennine landing site. Coordinates, landing date/time and returned sample mass traced to the NSSDCA Master Catalog spacecraft page for the Apollo 15 Lunar Module (primary NASA source, itself using LRO-derived coordinates), corroborated by the 2016-updated Wagner et al. (2017) LROC coordinate table. Physical-property fields (bulk density, friction angle, cohesion) traced to the Apollo 15 Preliminary Science Report (NASA SP-289) Chapter 7 'Soil-Mechanics Experiment' (Mitchell et al.), which states these as a headline result for 'station 8' and as a site-wide density range; none of the three stored numbers match the source's stated values, which are consistently higher (density ~2 vs 1.7 g/cm3; friction ~50 vs 48.1°; cohesion ~1.0 vs 0.77 kPa). Description was split into three separate factual claims (LRV first-use; Apennine Front sampling; Hadley Rille sampling), each independently supported.

check.notes:
I re-opened every document. Findings that change the reader's result:

1. The stored coordinates for L16, L17, L20 and L21 all come from NASA Solar System Exploration 'In Depth' pages, not from Wikipedia or an assumed pre-2016 NSSDCA version.
- L16: 0°41'S, 56°18'E.
- L17: 38°17'N, 35°W.

- L21: 25°51'N, 30°27'E.
These are the old nominal Soviet landing coordinates. LROC (Wagner et al.) has since replaced them with the values the reader quotes, so every 'differs' verdict still holds.

2. The L21 R7 mention_quote, and the L21 lat quote, splice a Wikipedia/In Depth clause ('between Mare Serenitatis and the Taurus Mountains') onto the NSSDCA sentence.

3. L20 samples_returned (55 g) is contradicted twice: NSSDCA says 30 g, and Lunar Sourcebook Table 2.1 says '(30 g)'. The reader missed the Sourcebook.

4. L16 cohesion 3.81 equals the mean of the five non-zero Gasteiner entries (3.812). It is the same undisclosed averaging as L16 bulk_density and friction_angle, L17 friction_angle and cohesion, and L20 bulk_density. I reproduced all of those means exactly.

5. Gasteiner's Luna 16 rows include five Jaffe 1973 rows. Those are Oceanus Procellarum (Apollo 12/Surveyor 3) soil, not Luna 16, so the stored L16 averages mix in another mission's data.

6. L17 and L21 strength values from Gasteiner (22.5°, 5 kPa, identical in both rows) conflict with Sourcebook Table 9.11: Lunokhod I ranges and a Lunokhod 1 and 2 average of 0.4 kPa / 40°, estimated. For L17, which has no clean single-source value, I recommend leaving these fields empty rather than correcting them.

7. L13 bulk_density 0.8 is what the sources state, but the same Sourcebook passage records Scott (1968) disputing it.

8. The Barsukov 1977 LPSC paper that Gasteiner cites for the Luna 24 density does not contain a density figure.

9. Sourcebook page locations are off by one to two pages for the prose quotes: the Luna 13 prose is on p.483 and the Luna 16 prose on p.485.

reading.notes:
Scope: only the 7 requested ids (S1, S3, CE3, CE4, CE5, CE6, CH3), all "site" entities (no "listed_sources" field present for any of them; none are sample entities, so no oxide/mineral/sample-field rows apply).

Methodology: read stored values from moon-entities-2026-09-25.json; for coordinates/dates I preferred a document I could open and quote verbatim (Wikipedia infobox text, mission reports, or peer-reviewed papers), then cross-checked against the LROC "Spacecraft Related Coordinates" table (which republishes Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283) and, for CE3/CH3 physical properties, against the Gasteiner et al. 2026 open dataset (GitHub CSV), which names each value's primary source. Where that primary source was itself paywalled (Dong & Fang 2016, Icarus, for CE3 bulk density; Mathew & Prasad 2025, Adv. Space Res., for CH3 bulk density) I documented the access attempts (Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar, ScienceDirect, ResearchGate, ProQuest, CORE) and, where a substitute open primary-ish source existed (a closely related, open-access ChaSTE paper for CH3), reported what that source actually states rather than silently trusting the compilation.

Surveyor soil-mechanics fields (friction_angle, cohesion) for S1 and S3: these could not be traced to any opened source at the exact stored precision (41.7°/4.52 kPa for S1; 42°/0.47 kPa for S3), despite checking the Surveyor I Mission Report (JPL TR 32-1023), the Surveyor-3-specific Scott & Roberson 1968 JGR paper (including its Table 5 "Soil Property Calculations" and Table 4 "Bearing Test Results"), and Lunar Sourcebook Table 9.11/9.12. I reported them as "differs", quoting the best matching statement each source does make (a range for S1; a specific density-paired estimate for S3), rather than silently forcing a match or marking outright "not_found", since a specific, on-topic document value does exist for each field — it just is not the stored number.
